claims: An immaculate inning in baseball occurs when a pitcher strikes out all three batters in a single inning using exactly nine pitches.
An immaculate inning requires 3 strikeouts, 9 pitches, 9 strikes.
Immaculate innings have occurred over 100 times in MLB history.
John Clarkson of the Boston Beaneaters threw the first recorded immaculate inning on June 4, 1889.
Michael Soroka of the Arizona Diamondbacks achieved an immaculate inning on March 30, 2026, against the Detroit Tigers.
Mason Miller achieved an immaculate inning in 2025.
Andrew Kittredge achieved an immaculate inning in 2025.
Only Sandy Koufax, Chris Sale, and Max Scherzer have accomplished an immaculate inning three times.
Nolan Ryan and Kevin Gausman are the only pitchers to have achieved an immaculate inning in both the American League and the National League.
